verdict.rationale: Auth0 documents machine-to-machine client credentials (Client ID/Secret exchanged for an access token) and authorization via scopes and granular permissions that explicitly covers M2M communications. Its AI offering also claims a unique identity per agent and delegated OAuth access that avoids broad, unrestricted access. Together these support issuing least-privilege credentials to an agent, but the evidence stitches separate pages together rather than documenting an end-to-end flow for scoping an agent's credentials. missing for 10: explicit first-party docs on granting a per-agent M2M client only selected API scopes, credential lifecycle details (rotation, expiry, revocation), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Handle authorization using scopes and granular permissions, whether it's for first-party apps, third-party integrations, or Machine-to-Machine communications.
Applications authenticate themselves to Auth0 via their Client Id and Client Secret. Auth0 verifies the information and responds with an Access Token.
Give each agent a unique digital identity for more secure access to APIs, apps, and MCP servers.
preventing agents from having broad, unrestricted access to user data.
